subject: Customer Q: data processing, retention, and non-training commitment
messages:
From: Priya Sharma <priya@starlighthealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: security@starlighthealth.com
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 13:12:00 -0400
Subject: Quick Q on data processing & retention — do you train on customer data?

Hi Ben,

Hope you’re well. Our security team flagged two items during our vendor review and I wanted to confirm directly:

1) Training on customer data: our policy requires vendors to confirm they do not use customer data to train or improve models unless explicitly contracted. Can you confirm Redwood’s stance here?

2) Retention windows: we need clarity on default retention times for request logs, prompts, and any persisted artifacts tied to an account, plus any deletion workflows (self-serve vs. support-assisted).

We’re in a tight procurement window and these answers will help speed legal review. If you have a short one-pager or SOC2 scope that calls this out, that would be great.

Thanks,
Priya Sharma
Security Lead
Starlight Health

[attachment: starlight-soc2-scope.pdf (referenced)]

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@starlighthealth.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Jul 2028 14:05:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q on data processing & retention — do you train on customer data?

Hi Priya — thanks for flagging this and for the SOC2 scope. Short answer up front: we do not use customer data from your inference requests to train or update our public or internal model weights unless you explicitly opt in via a contract addendum.

A few clarifying bullets so your legal/supply chain folks have precise wording:
- Non-training commitment: by default, request payloads (prompts, completions, metadata) submitted to Redwood’s hosted service are not used to train models. We store some telemetry and logging for operational purposes (latency, error rates, billing).
- Retention tiers: operational logs (token-level billing, traces) are retained for 90 days by default; aggregated telemetry is kept for 24 months. Customers on Enterprise Dedicated or Private can customize retention windows or configure automatic deletion policies.
- Deletion paths:
  * Self-service: in the Console you can purge stored logs for your account; this will remove request payloads and associated traces within 24 hours of the purge action for hosted accounts.
  * Support-assisted: for regulated accounts we provide scoped deletion and certificate-of-deletion upon request; this is performed under a signed data-removal SOW to ensure auditability.
- Exceptions: derived telemetry used for capacity planning (e.g., sequence length histograms) is aggregated and non-identifiable; we don’t retain raw user prompts in these aggregates.

I’m looping Laura (Legal) and Vivek (Head of Product) to add any contractual language and confirm operational timelines. Will attach the retention matrix and a short policy excerpt.

Next steps: Laura — can you confirm language we can include in contract (non-training clause + deletion SLA)? Priya — I can schedule a 20-min sync tomorrow if helpful.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Exec | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 415-555-0192

[attachment: retention-matrix.csv (summary of retention tiers)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Priya Sharma <priya@starlighthealth.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Cc: vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Jul 2028 09:18:00 -0400
Subject: Re: Quick Q on data processing & retention — do you train on customer data?

Hi Priya — adding a precise contract-ready statement below you can drop into your vendor questionnaire. Ben, feel free to use this when drafting the clause.

"Redwood Inference does not use Customer Content (including prompts, responses, or other inference request data) to train, improve, or tune Redwood’s public or internal models unless Customer has explicitly provided written consent via a mutually executed agreement. Redwood may retain operational logs and metadata for service delivery, billing, and security purposes as described in the Service Data Retention Schedule. Redwood will, upon Customer’s request, delete Customer Content and provide confirmation in accordance with the agreed deletion SLA."

Notes and operational specifics:
- Hosted customers: default retention for request payloads is 90 days; deletion requests initiated via Console are propagated within 24 hours and completed within 72 hours in most regions.
- Dedicated customers: retention is configurable per contract; default on-commit is 30 days for debug logs, can be set to 0.
- Private / On-prem: data residency and retention are controlled by the customer; Redwood’s control plane may store pointers/logs depending on deployment (documented in the Private deployment addendum).
- Audit artifacts: for SOC 2 or procurement reviews, we can provide redacted logs and a certificate-of-deletion when support-assisted removal is performed.

If you want, I can produce a short addendum (one paragraph) with the non-training commitment and deletion SLA for your legal team to attach to the MSA.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy | Redwood Inference
